title: Treasury yields around speeches by the Federal Reserve Chair
method: Historical release times are taken from the dated delivery instructions on the first page of the FRASER transcript when the Board index omits a time. The pre-speech change runs from the fifth prior Treasury fixing to the final pre-release fixing (four successive changes). The 2s10s spread is the ten-year par yield minus the two-year par yield.

A speech before the approximately 15:30 ET Treasury fixing uses the previous trading day's fixing as its baseline. A later speech uses the same day's fixing and the next available fixing. Non-quote days are bracketed by the adjacent available fixings.

When a trading-day release time is missing, the daily change describes the calendar date only. The change is excluded from the event-window statistics. Speeches listed at exactly the fixing time are also excluded.

The matched sample has a unique speech per fixing interval and excludes FOMC decisions within that interval. A speech or decision with unknown or exactly-at-fixing timing on either boundary can overlap both adjacent windows. Other releases and trading still contribute. The one-calendar-day sensitivity additionally drops holiday and weekend spans.

The observed short-window readings and September meeting prices identify their own instruments and source windows. Daily par yields contain term premia and rate expectations across maturities. They do not identify meeting-specific probabilities.

The Atlanta Fed Market Probability Tracker uses CME options to estimate distributions for average compounded SOFR over a three-month reference window. We select the nearest reference window starting on or after the speech, and the last price date strictly before the speech. The change compares the same reference window on the fifth and last prior price dates. Above/below probabilities refer to the then-current fed funds target range. These are educational calculations from daily option data.
NBER contractions run from the month after a dated peak through the month of its trough. These are retrospective labels.

75 bp hike probability, 56.5% before and 60.5% afterwards.
meetingPricing.reading: With 50 and 75 bp as the two outcomes, implied tightening rose from 64.13 to 65.13 bp. The source gives no quote times, so other news could enter the 1.00 bp change.

records.instrument: September meeting expected change in the fed funds target

meetingPricing.beforeAndAfter: 25 bp hike probability, 19.5% at 10:00 and 21.5% at 10:20 ET.
meetingPricing.reading: Powell spoke at 10:05. Across this 20-minute window the expected move rose from +4.88 to +5.38 bp. By 15:00 it was back to +4.88 bp. The initial repricing was half a basis point and had unwound by mid-afternoon.

meetingPricing.beforeAndAfter: The reported probability of a 25 bp cut fell 0.5 percentage points before the speech, from 76.5% on 16 August to 76% on 22 August.
meetingPricing.reading: Market participants were already choosing between a 25 and 50 bp cut. Thursday’s probabilities implied 31.00 bp of easing. By Friday afternoon the reported probability of 50 bp was 36.5%, equivalent to 34.13 bp of easing. The additional 3.13 bp spans a prior-day to afternoon interval.

meetingPricing.beforeAndAfter: September cut probability, 75% the day before and 91.5% after the speech.
meetingPricing.reading: The reported probability rose 16.5 percentage points. The report gives the chance of a cut without a complete distribution by size, so the change is displayed in probability points. The interval includes overnight news.
